chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that they both asked him:
about eating the meat of domesticated donkeys. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade it, and forbade eating it on the day of Khayber.'
And he only forbade eating it at that time because it was the carriers of the people,
and the prohibition is only what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited in the Quran.

key_terms.حَمُولَةَ النَّاسِ: carriers of the people (beasts of burden)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet forbid eating donkeys if it is not explicitly in the Quran?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the distinction between temporary prohibition (haram li-ghayrihi) and permanent prohibition (haram li-dhatihi), noting that the ban on domesticated donkeys at Khayber was pragmatic due to their utility as transport. It reinforces the Shia principle that while the Prophet's prohibitions are binding, the ultimate source of absolute haram is the Quran, a view that supports the permissibility of other animals not explicitly banned in scripture.
